title: Magnetic fields
target: Interpret magnetic field patterns and compass direction.
criteria: Trace external field direction from north toward south.
Explain why field-line drawings are models.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Two bar magnets approach with south poles facing. What is expected?
options: They repel.
They attract.
Both poles turn electrically positive.
Only one magnet feels force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A bar magnet’s north end faces another magnet’s south end. What interaction is expected?
options: Attraction.
No force unless they touch.
Repulsion.
Creation of an isolated north pole.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Along the outside of a bar magnet, which direction convention do field arrows follow?
options: From south toward north.
Away from both poles to infinity only.
From north toward south.
Along the direction a negative electric charge must travel.
cpa.guide: Outside the magnet, arrows follow the north-seeking compass direction, north to south.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A compass is placed just outside a magnet’s north pole on its axis. Which way does the compass’s north-seeking end point in the magnet’s dominant field?
options: Always toward the ceiling.
Toward that north pole.
At right angles to every field line.
Away from that north pole.
cpa.guide: The external field emerges from the north pole; the compass north end aligns with it.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A drawing uses more closely spaced field lines near one location. What does that convention indicate?
options: More physical strings inside the magnet.
A stronger field there, using the same drawing convention.
A larger electric current is proved.
An exact numerical field value without a scale.
cpa.guide: Line density is a qualitative model of field strength, not a count of physical lines.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A student says a magnet has no field between the drawn lines. Which correction is best?
options: Adding ink would strengthen the actual magnet.
Field exists only at the poles’ surfaces.
The student is right because only ink carries the force.
Lines sample a continuous field; spaces in the drawing do not mean zero field.
cpa.guide: A field-line diagram is a representation; its drawn lines are not isolated physical objects.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
